title: Flight Compartment Side Window Surround — Gusset and Frame Corrosion Repair

ata.title: Flight Compartment Windows — Side Window Assembly

abstract: Repair of corrosion in the flight compartment side window surround gussets and frame, by blend-out or by gusset replacement, with the sealing that keeps the pressure boundary intact.

sections.purpose: This repair restores corrosion damage in the side window surround gussets and the adjacent frame, and re-establishes the sealing of the pressure boundary around the window.
sections.damage_assessment: Corrosion here nearly always starts at the lower corners, where condensation runs down the inside of the pane and collects at the seal. Remove the interior trim and look at both lower corners before anything else, even if the reported finding is elsewhere. Measure the remaining thickness on a grid at fifteen millimetre spacing; the gussets are thin and a loss that would be trivial on a frame is significant here. Check the drain path at the lower corner and record whether it is clear, because a blocked drain is the reason the corrosion is there and blending it out without clearing the drain simply resets the clock.
sections.repair_procedure: 1. Remove the interior trim and the window where the drawing requires it. 2. Clean the area and remove the protective scheme locally. 3. Measure the remaining thickness on the grid and record every reading. 4. Clear and prove the drain path at the lower corner before any repair work. 5. Where the loss is inside the blend limit, blend it out to a smooth radius and re-measure. 6. Where the loss exceeds the blend limit, remove the gusset D5610121193526 or D5610123688445 as applicable and install the replacement with the clip FJDE819380-76 as backing. 7. Do an eddy current inspection of every hole in the parent frame before any fastener is installed. 8. Install the fasteners LN740793K3 wet with sealant, with the washers AGS791298-9A under the heads and the spacers EN678326K8 where the drawing calls for them. 9. Restore the protective scheme over the whole repair. 10. Re-install the window with a new seal and torque the retainer in the marked sequence. 11. Apply the sealing compound at the pressure boundary in accordance with the drawing. 12. Do a pressurisation leak check at the window and record the leak rate.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a pressurisation leak check after the repair and record the leak rate; compare it against the pre-repair value where one exists. Do a detailed visual inspection of both lower corners and of the drain path at every C-check. Where a gusset was replaced, do an eddy current inspection of the attachment row every eight thousand flight cycles. Record the drain path condition every time, because a repair that recurs is a drainage finding and not a structural one.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Blend-out up to 10 per cent of nominal gusset thickness over an area not exceeding 2 500 square millimetres. Beyond that the gusset is replaced. Not more than two gussets replaced per window.

materials.description: GUSSET, SIDE WINDOW ASSEMBLY, SUB-ASSY, RH

type_data.fastener_pattern: Single row at 16 mm pitch with 12 mm edge distance; every fastener installed wet with sealant and sealed over the head
type_data.fatigue_life_note: The gusset replacement carries no fatigue life limit but requires an eddy current inspection of the attachment row every 8 000 flight cycles and a pressurisation leak check at every C-check.
